title: A Survey of Large Language Models
actual_read_scope: Read the arXiv abstract/metadata and experimental HTML v19 table of contents; read the relevant parts of IV-A1 (specialized pretraining data), IV-B (architecture/configuration/decoding), V-A3/V-A4 (instruction tuning effects), VI-C (CoT), VII-A3 (complex reasoning), VIII-B (specific domains), IX-D (inference efficiency and algorithm-level optimization), IX-H (long-CoT reasoning), and the cited-reference entries used below. Did not read any cited original paper.

routes.problem: Autoregressive decoding spends one memory-bound step per generated token.
routes.mechanism: The survey separates prefill from autoregressive decoding, models arithmetic intensity, and identifies decoding as memory-wall/data-transfer limited; it then groups system and algorithm optimizations.
routes.inference_token_connection: Direct deployment route: reducing verification steps, skipped layers, or generated steps can lower wall-clock/token cost while retaining output quality, but the survey mostly reports speed/throughput rather than quality-versus-token curves.

routes.problem: Every token need not be generated by the largest model or by every layer.
routes.mechanism: Speculative decoding drafts several tokens with a small model and verifies with the large model; cascades route easy requests to cheaper models; early exit/mixture-of-depths skip computation conditionally.
routes.inference_token_connection: Direct for token-efficient serving when acceptance/exit decisions preserve task quality; evidence in this survey is speed-oriented and does not establish a universal token-quality frontier.

routes.problem: Long-CoT reasoning improves difficult-task search but may spend excessive tokens on easy questions.
routes.mechanism: Long CoT adds reflection, backtracking, verification, planning, and exploration; the survey explicitly notes a tendency after SFT to default to long-CoT mode even for simple problems.
routes.inference_token_connection: Direct diagnostic for adaptive stopping/short-vs-long routing: response length is a visible resource signal, but no calibrated optimal stopping curve is supplied.
routes.survey_locator: §IX-H1, §IX-H3 (especially the downside paragraph after the 3.9K-data result)

routes.problem: Pretraining and post-training data shape whether a model can solve complex reasoning or specialized tasks.
routes.mechanism: The survey links multilingual/scientific/code corpora and continual mathematical pretraining to downstream capabilities; instruction tuning generalizes to unseen tasks and can transfer across languages.
routes.inference_token_connection: Indirect: stronger representations may reduce retries or required reasoning tokens, but the survey does not measure token savings or short-answer parity.

routes.problem: Model internals and decoding choices affect factuality, faithfulness, and explanation behavior.
routes.mechanism: The survey discusses layer-wise contrastive decoding (DoLa), truth-correlated attention heads (ITI), self-consistency, tool/code execution, and reasoning-path consistency.
routes.inference_token_connection: Indirect/direct only for decoding-time selection: these can change how many candidate paths or verification tokens are generated, but the survey gives no redundancy diagnostic or token-normalized explanation measure.

candidates.title: Fast inference from transformers via speculative decoding
candidates.authors: Y. Leviathan, M. Kalman, Y. Matias
candidates.reason: Draft-and-verify reduces serial large-model generation steps; the survey reports this route as inference acceleration without a token-quality curve.

candidates.title: Accelerating large language model decoding with speculative sampling
candidates.reason: A second draft/verification formulation cited for the survey's 2×–3× speedup discussion.

candidates.title: SpecInfer: accelerating generative LLM serving with speculative inference and token tree verification
candidates.reason: Token-tree verification is a concrete route to amortize multiple candidate tokens per target-model pass.

candidates.title: Accelerating LLM inference with staged speculative decoding
candidates.reason: Staged drafting is cited as a further reduction of serial decoding overhead.

candidates.title: FrugalGPT: how to use large language models while reducing cost and improving performance
candidates.authors: L. Chen, M. Zaharia, J. Zou
candidates.reason: Routes requests through models of increasing capability and bypasses later models when an answer is reliable; directly relevant to conditional token/compute allocation.

candidates.title: Large language model cascades with mixture of thoughts representations for cost-efficient reasoning
candidates.authors: M. Yue, J. Zhao, M. Zhang, L. Du, Z. Yao
candidates.reason: Uses self-consistency to decide when a larger model is needed for reasoning; relevant to adaptive reasoning-token budgets.

candidates.title: Medusa: simple LLM inference acceleration framework with multiple decoding heads
candidates.reason: Additional heads predict later tokens in parallel; the survey notes quality trade-offs and verification use.

candidates.title: Mixture-of-depths: dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
candidates.reason: Dynamically skips selected layers per input, a representation-level compute reduction during decoding; token-count effect is unreported here.

candidates.title: Imitate, explore, and self-improve: a reproduction report on slow-thinking reasoning systems
candidates.reason: The survey reports 3.9K distilled long-CoT examples, cross-domain transfer to physics/chemistry, and default long reasoning on simple prompts.

candidates.title: DeepSeek-R1: incentivizing reasoning capability in LLMs via reinforcement learning
candidates.reason: Cited as evidence that RL and distilled long-CoT can elicit extended reasoning; the survey emphasizes response-length monitoring, not a short-answer efficiency curve.

candidates.title: Kimi k1.5: scaling reinforcement learning with llms
candidates.reason: Cited as another long-CoT RL system comparable to o1; deployment token efficiency is not quantified in this survey.

candidates.title: Language models are multilingual chain-of-thought reasoners
candidates.reason: Directly relevant to multilingual CoT capability and parity; the survey does not report language-specific token lengths or token-normalized accuracy.

candidates.title: SciBench: evaluating college-level scientific problem-solving abilities of large language models
candidates.reason: A cited science-reasoning benchmark useful for measuring quality at fixed or varying reasoning-token budgets; the survey does not provide such a curve.

candidates.title: OceanGPT: A large language model for ocean science tasks
candidates.reason: Representative domain model cited under specific-domain applications; no deployment token evidence is given.

candidates.title: Do emergent abilities of large language models exist? A closer look at the claims and evidence
candidates.authors: R. Schaeffer, B. Miranda, S. Koyejo
candidates.reason: The survey cites this as a critique of emergent-ability discontinuities; it is relevant to avoiding false claims that larger representations automatically create token-efficient reasoning.

classification_gaps: No dedicated taxonomy of inference-token efficiency, overthinking, token redundancy, sponge attacks, or adversarial prompts designed to induce long outputs.
Interpretability is discussed through mechanisms such as attention heads/layers and decoding, but no operational redundancy diagnostic or explanation-token accounting is supplied.
Multilingual and scientific material is organized as data sources, benchmarks, or applications, not as language/domain-specific quality-versus-token frontiers.
evidence_conflicts: The survey reports speedups, throughput, arithmetic intensity, and qualitative long-CoT benefits; these are not equivalent to fewer generated tokens at matched quality.
Long-CoT sections argue for more test-time computation on difficult tasks while also noting long-CoT defaulting on easy tasks; the adaptive boundary remains unresolved.
training_only_or_compute_only: Scaling laws, pretraining FLOPs, distributed training, and most memory/compression discussions are compute or deployment-memory topics rather than evidence of fewer reasoning tokens.
Flash-Decoding, PagedAttention, continuous batching, and quantization reduce transfer or memory cost; they do not by themselves reduce the number of output tokens.
gaps_conflicts.security_resource_waste: No occurrences of sponge, overthinking, token-wasting, or adversarial-output resource exhaustion were found in the read v19 HTML. The survey mentions red teaming and adversarial prompts only as safety/alignment context, without token-cost measurements.
gaps_conflicts.update_cutoff: v19 (2026-03-18), checked 2026-09-09; long-CoT coverage includes 2024–2025 references, but no post-2026-03 survey revision was found on the arXiv record.
